question: Japan: if a bank or payment system fails, who takes the loss, in what order?
answer: On the Japan money map (as of September 15, 2026), a failure moves through 5 separate steps: what sets it off (Ordinary liquidity stress, Operational outage, Systemic failure classification); the private first response (Commercial banks, Japan Securities Clearing Corporation, Zengin System and More Time, FMI default waterfalls); the Bank of Japan's liquidity step (BOJ Policy Board, BOJ current-account balances, BOJ-NET Funds Transfer System, BOJ Article 33 lending, BOJ Article 37 outage lending, BOJ Article 38 special support), which lends against collateral and does not cover a final loss; resolution (Cabinet and Prime Minister, Financial Services Agency, Deposit Insurance Corporation of Japan, TLAC and creditor loss, Deposit protection and transfer); and where the loss finally lands (Fraud compensation and restitution, JPYSC trust stablecoin, Possible retail CBDC, Industry contributions, Conditional fiscal subsidy or guarantee). Public money is a last, conditional step that needs legal and budget approval.

sections.title: The loss order, step by step
sections.sub: Operational recovery, liquidity, resolution, creditor loss, industry mutualisation and fiscal support are separate rungs.

items.title: Ordinary liquidity stress
items.sub: Solvent participant needs temporary funding
kv: A funding shortfall or market-liquidity need that may be bridged against eligible collateral.
What it does to the books
Creates a temporary cash need, not necessarily an economic loss.
Liquidity stress must not be relabeled insolvency without loss evidence.
Participant liquidity, collateral and BOJ facility records.

items.title: Operational outage
items.sub: Temporary inability to settle
kv: A computer or operational disruption can prevent an otherwise eligible institution from making payments.
What it does to the books
Creates a timing and liquidity gap even if assets exceed liabilities.
An outage is not itself credit loss or insolvency.

sources.label: BOJ-NET Funds Transfer System PFMI Disclosure

items.title: Systemic failure classification
items.sub: Private failure threatens financial-system continuity
kv: Marks the legal and policy threshold at which ordinary private treatment may be insufficient for stability.
What it does to the books
Can open extraordinary liquidity, resolution, guarantees or conditional fiscal pathways.
Legal capacity and classification are not evidence of current activation or realized public cost.
Government, Policy Board, FSA and DICJ decisions.

items.title: Commercial banks
items.sub: Dominant issuers of spendable deposit money
kv: Issue deposits, keep customer ledgers, participate in payment and securities systems and intermediate JGB and credit markets.
What it does to the books
Receive reserve interest, reprice deposits and loans, hold securities and absorb first-round income, funding and duration effects.
A bank deposit is denominated in yen but is not the customer's BOJ reserve account.
Bank core ledgers, accounts and prudential reports.

sources.label: BOJ-NET Funds Transfer System PFMI Disclosure

items.title: Japan Securities Clearing Corporation
items.sub: CCP novation, margin, default and liquidity controls
kv: Clears eligible JGB and other transactions, becoming central counterparty and applying margin and default resources.
What it does to the books
Mutualizes defined exposures while keeping default-loss resources separate from liquidity facilities.
JSCC clearing does not make JSCC the sovereign debtor or the issuer of yen settlement money.
JSCC positions, margin and default-management records.

items.title: Zengin System and More Time
items.sub: Bank transfer messaging, RTGS/DNS and 24/7 interface
kv: Routes domestic credit transfers and calculates or submits interbank settlement positions under distinct large- and small-value designs.
What it does to the books
Creates interbank receivables/payables and contains pending exposure with collateral, caps and participant resources.
Customer availability can precede BOJ settlement; the message is not reserve money.

items.title: FMI default waterfalls
items.sub: Defaulter resources before mutualized survivor loss
kv: Allocates clearing or payment-system default loss through collateral, participant resources, operator capital and defined mutualization.
What it does to the books
Private resources absorb loss while separate liquidity facilities preserve scheduled settlement.
Liquidity facilities and loss-compensation resources are not interchangeable.

items.title: BOJ Policy Board
items.sub: Monetary-policy and special-support judgment
kv: Decides monetary policy, JGB-purchase frameworks and BOJ judgment under exceptional-support powers.
What it does to the books
Can change BOJ asset and liability flows but does not erase the government's JGB obligation.
Policy judgment is distinct from fiscal authority, agency execution and settlement finality.
MPM decisions, BOJ rules and Policy Board resolutions.

sources.label: BOJ Reduction of JGB Purchase Amount

items.title: BOJ current-account balances
items.sub: Wholesale yen settlement asset
kv: Liabilities of the BOJ to eligible account holders used for final wholesale yen settlement.
What it does to the books
Move among participant accounts and earn remuneration under applicable tiers; customers generally do not hold them directly.
Reserve movement is not identical to the gross customer-payment amount or the customer's deposit claim.

sources.label: BOJ-NET Funds Transfer System PFMI Disclosure

items.title: BOJ-NET Funds Transfer System
items.sub: Final wholesale yen settlement
kv: Debits and credits BOJ current accounts and provides finality when the BOJ confirms and records the transfer.
What it does to the books
Discharges wholesale yen obligations in central-bank money; collateralized intraday credit supports liquidity.
After finality, error or fraud ordinarily requires compensation, restitution or a new transfer—not narrative cancellation.
BOJ current-account ledger and BOJ-NET confirmation.

sources.label: BOJ-NET Funds Transfer System PFMI Disclosure

items.title: BOJ Article 33 lending
items.sub: Ordinary collateralized central-bank credit
kv: Provides credit against eligible collateral within the BOJ's ordinary business framework.
What it does to the books
BOJ loan asset and participant reserve liability rise; collateral secures the exposure.
Collateralized liquidity does not compensate a terminal solvency loss.

sources.label: BOJ Review of Resolvability and TBTF

items.title: BOJ Article 37 outage lending
items.sub: Temporary credit for accidental operational disruption
kv: Bridges temporary payment-system inability caused by unexpected operational trouble.
What it does to the books
Creates temporary BOJ credit and reserves to preserve settlement continuity.
The power addresses outage liquidity, not general recapitalization.
BOJ authorization, loan and repayment records.

items.title: BOJ Article 38 special support
items.sub: Government request plus Policy Board necessity judgment
kv: Permits special BOJ business necessary to maintain financial-system stability under statutory conditions.
What it does to the books
Can create extraordinary BOJ exposure, whose realized repayment or loss remains a later empirical question.
Exceptional authority is not a standing guarantee and not evidence that it is presently in use.
Government request, Policy Board decision and facility accounts.

sources.label: BOJ Review of Resolvability and TBTF

items.title: Cabinet and Prime Minister
items.sub: Appointments and systemic statutory gates
kv: Participates in appointment, accountability and extraordinary Deposit Insurance Act decisions.
What it does to the books
Can activate public-law continuity measures; activation is not evidence that fiscal loss has already occurred.
The Cabinet does not replace the BOJ Policy Board's monetary-policy decision or MOF's operating books.
Cabinet decisions, orders and systemic-measure notices.

items.title: Financial Services Agency
items.sub: Supervision, perimeter and resolution preparation
kv: Supervises regulated firms, defines prudential and conduct expectations and prepares resolution pathways.
What it does to the books
Constrains capital, liquidity, claim treatment and loss capacity without becoming every firm's debtor.
Regulation is not ownership, settlement, deposit issuance or a guarantee of zero loss.
Supervisory guidance, registrations and resolution plans.

items.title: Deposit Insurance Corporation of Japan
items.sub: Deposit protection, transfer and resolution assistance
kv: Administers insured-deposit protection, financial assistance, bridge mechanisms and statutory resolution funding.
What it does to the books
Can borrow, receive BOJ temporary cash-flow loans and mobilize industry or conditional fiscal funding through legal gates.
DICJ resolution assistance is distinct from BOJ lender-of-last-resort liquidity.
DICJ records and Deposit Insurance Act processes.

sources.label: BOJ Review of Resolvability and TBTF

items.title: TLAC and creditor loss
items.sub: Large-group continuity with holding-company loss absorption
kv: Transfers losses up to the domestic resolution entity, writes down capital and leaves external TLAC creditors in the non-viable holding company.
What it does to the books
Equity, AT1/T2 and eligible creditors absorb losses while critical operations can move to a bridge.
A preferred strategy is case-specific and not proof of a current resolution event.
Firm resolution plans, write-down decisions and insolvency records.

items.title: Deposit protection and transfer
items.sub: Payment deposits fully protected; other covered deposits capped
kv: Protects defined deposit claims and can transfer them into a continuing or bridge institution.
What it does to the books
DICJ and insured institutions fund covered payouts or assistance under statutory rules; uncovered excess can remain at risk.
Common yen denomination does not make every bank or digital claim equally insured.
Bank books, depositor classifications and DICJ resolution records.

items.title: Fraud compensation and restitution
items.sub: A new recovery path after final payment
kv: Uses bank compensation rules or statutory criminal-account procedures to restore some victim value after the original payment.
What it does to the books
Creates compensation or distributes residual frozen funds; recovery can be partial and delayed.
Recovery does not rewrite the historical BOJ finality event.
Bank, DICJ, police and statutory restitution records.

items.title: JPYSC trust stablecoin
items.sub: Trust-beneficiary claim with segregated reserves
kv: Represents a specified-trust beneficiary claim whose reserves can include permitted deposits and short sovereign assets.
What it does to the books
Reserve mix can migrate from demand deposits into term deposits or short JGBs; tokenholder does not own a BOJ claim.
One-yen denomination does not supply deposit insurance or guarantee instant par recovery in failure.
Trust books, on-chain state and redemption records.

items.title: Possible retail CBDC
items.sub: The only studied direct public retail BOJ claim
kv: Tests a two-tier design in which the public instrument would be a direct liability of the BOJ distributed through intermediaries.
What it does to the books
Would change the holder's debtor from a bank to the BOJ if authorized and issued; no public-value issuance exists at cutoff.
Technical readiness is not legislation, issuance, adoption or a settled failure constitution.
Pilot central/customer ledgers, not a live legal-tender ledger.

items.title: Industry contributions
items.sub: Financial-sector funding before conditional fiscal subsidy
kv: Recoups defined resolution costs across covered institutions under Deposit Insurance Act contribution rules.
What it does to the books
Moves cost from the failed firm toward the surviving industry perimeter.
Industry mutualization is not the same as taxpayer absorption.

items.title: Conditional fiscal subsidy or guarantee
items.sub: Public loss only through legal and budget gates
kv: Supports systemic continuity when industry-only funding would itself threaten orderly credit or markets, subject to statutory and Diet constraints.
What it does to the books
Can convert contingent public capacity into realized fiscal exposure.
The existence of a backstop is not evidence that every private loss has already become public.
Budget, guarantee, subsidy and DICJ accounts.

uncertain: A visual projection of the completed Layers 0–8 and system-wide synthesis. It distinguishes observed balance-sheet movement, operating infrastructure, legal capacity, pilots, unresolved design and the retired JGB–HKD adapter. Spatial proximity is not ownership or causation.
The steps are the map's reading of Japanese law and practice; no Japanese failure since the cutoff has tested this order.
